prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, using designed small molecules to direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to selected proteins

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is a new chemical modality, not just a new drug. A small molecule is designed to bring an E3 ligase and a target protein together, and the mechanism can be examined in physical terms: ternary-complex cooperativity, linker geometry, and the kinetics of ubiquitin transfer. That is the kind of molecular design the chemistry prize has honoured before. The concept dates from Crews and Deshaies around 2001. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures turned it into a general, drug-like platform that independent groups reproduced. A Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli configuration has a coherent story from concept through structural rationalisation. The field is large, mechanistically well understood, and has many compounds in clinical trials. It also received the strongest opening support in this committee, with four first-place rankings, but I am arguing from the chemistry and not from the vote count.
statement.case_against: No bifunctional degrader has yet reached approval, so the clinical payoff is still a forward-looking claim and the prize could look early. Any three-person set leaves out a decisive strand. The cereblon and thalidomide mechanism (Handa, Ito, Kim) is the origin of the molecular-glue half and is arguably the most surprising discovery in the field. Sakamoto's role in the first PROTAC and Gray's covalent and kinase-directed degraders are also real claims. If the committee cannot accept a configuration that splits PROTACs and glues, or cannot settle the allocation, a mature and cleanly attributed alternative such as Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B002) is the safer choice.

responses.point: Daniel ranks B023 first but proposes Crews, Deshaies and Handa, so that the original PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism behind molecular glues are both credited.
responses.response: I take the point that the glue mechanism is a distinct and surprising discovery, and omitting it will be criticised. But Handa's contribution is the identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target. That is a target-identification result in the biology of a single drug class. The PROTAC strand is a general design principle for any target. For a citation about a chemical modality I prefer Ciulli, whose VHL ligands and ternary-complex work generalised the idea, over Handa. I would not object strongly to Handa if the committee decides the prize should be anchored in the thalidomide mechanism. I do not think that choice is clearly better, and it should be decided explicitly and not by default.

responses.point: Xiaodong ranks B023 only fourth. She sees the science as well confirmed but regards recognition as possibly premature because no approved degrader exists, and she notes that Handa and Ito's cereblon work is a separate part of the discovery.
responses.response: The timing concern is fair and is my main reservation. I would answer that the Nobel test is the confirmed scientific discovery, not an approval. Independent laboratories have confirmed the mechanism in detail, and the ternary-complex chemistry is understood at the structural level. We have not waited for approval before in comparable cases. I agree with her that the cereblon work is a separate strand. If she thinks it needs its own recognition, I would like to hear how she would configure the prize without a three-name cap forcing an arbitrary cut. I do not think a two-part prize with separate PROTAC and glue citations would be coherent, since both rest on the same induced-proximity idea.

responses.point: Peter ranks proton-coupled electron transfer (B028) first as a mature, unifying concept with textbook status in both enzymes and electrocatalysis, and ranks B023 third because clinical validation is still emerging.
responses.response: I agree that B028 is scientifically mature and fundamental, and its theory strand, Hammes-Schiffer's multistate PCET theory, is close to my own computational work. I find it a strong candidate and have listed it as an alternative. My reservation is attribution: it joins molecular electrocatalysis (Nocera, Meyer), physical-organic thermochemistry (Mayer) and theory (Hammes-Schiffer) that are only loosely linked. A citation might read as a list of three different things. I would like Peter to say what single sentence unifies them. If he can, B028 becomes much more competitive with B023.

responses.point: Peter Somfai ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B002) first as a general, ligand-controlled method with clean two-person credit (Buchwald, Hartwig) and calls it fully mature and overdue. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a non-general precursor.
responses.response: I largely agree on the science and on the attribution; B002 is the cleanest two-person case on the shortlist and my second choice. My hesitation is the same one I raised in my opening ballot: the 2010 cross-coupling prize covered the C-C chapter, and the committee has to ask whether a second prize on closely related Pd chemistry is the best use of a scarce slot. Mechanistically important is not the same as conceptually new. Degraders open a different modality. I would not stand in the way if the committee judged that overdue methodology should win, and B002 is my first fallback.

uncertainties: Whether the committee wants a three-person PROTAC set (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) or one anchored on cereblon (Handa), and how to credit Sakamoto, Ito, Kim and Gray.
Whether a prize before the first approved degrader is premature, and whether I am underweighting that risk.
Whether the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands count as one discovery or two for citation purposes.
Whether the 2010 cross-coupling prize should weigh against B002 (Buchwald and Hartwig).
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. None of the shortlisted candidates is a collaborator, supervisor or Uppsala colleague. My postdoc with Arieh Warshel concerned EVB simulation and he is not on the shortlist. My research field overlaps with the computational side of B028 (Hammes-Schiffer), but that is scientific proximity, not a personal tie. I have served on the committee with Peter Brzezinski since 2015, which is not a conflict.
